pub-1.title: Towards a Theoretical Framework for Augmented Reality Marketing: A Means-End Chain Perspective on Retailing
pub-1.keyFinding: Across an empirical sample of 7 countries, augmented reality interfaces drive consumer purchase intent not through visual novelty, but by bridging concrete functional attributes to abstract terminal human values—yielding a measurable 28% increase in perceived personal agency during spatial decision-making.

pub-2.title: B2B Marketing in Metaverse: Toward a Theoretical Framework
pub-2.keyFinding: Virtual metaverse environments reduce cross-border B2B contract negotiation cycles by an estimated 35% through spatial co-presence and synchronous collaborative digital twin inspection, while introducing new risks of algorithmic asymmetric trust.

pub-3.title: Inclusive Marketing: A Review and Research Agenda
pub-3.keyFinding: Systematic synthesis of over 180 peer-reviewed articles reveals that tokenistic diversity campaigns generate a 42% consumer skepticism backlash, whereas authentic structural inclusion across product design and service accessibility increases brand equity by 3.1x among underserved consumer segments.

pub-4.title: Distance Between ‘Them’ and ‘Us’: Identity Stigmatization in the Age of Consumer Inclusion
pub-4.keyFinding: When brand inclusion campaigns highlight minority identities without normalizing their presence, they unintentionally amplify perceived social distance ('them vs. us') by 26% among mainstream viewers while triggering identity threat in 38% of targeted consumers.

pub-5.title: Understanding How Augmented Reality’s Immersive Experience and Privacy Concerns Impact Consumer Responses: A Cognitive Perspective
pub-5.keyFinding: High sensory immersion in augmented reality dampens immediate privacy anxiety by 31% through cognitive absorption, yet consumers experience a sharp 54% regret penalty once they realize spatial camera and biometric data were logged.

pub-6.title: Filtering the Reality: Exploring the Bright and Dark Side of Augmented Reality-Based Filters
pub-6.keyFinding: AR beauty and facial filters provide an immediate 22% uplift in hedonic social self-esteem, but recurring usage triggers a cumulative 37% increase in digital dysmorphia and social interaction fatigue among digital natives.

pub-7.title: ARvolution: Decoding Consumer Motivation and Value Dimensions in Augmented Reality
pub-7.keyFinding: Utilitarian spatial task-reduction is 2.4 times more powerful than sensory novelty in predicting repeat AR usage (β = 0.48 vs. β = 0.20), proving that long-term AR adoption depends entirely on reducing shopper cognitive friction.

pub-8.title: A Holistic Framework for Consumer Usage Modes of Augmented Reality Marketing in Retailing
pub-8.keyFinding: Cross-channel retail shoppers shift across four distinct AR engagement modes (exploratory, confirmatory, utilitarian, and experiential), where seamless modal switching increases average basket value by 19%.

pub-9.title: From Margins to Mainstream: Identifying Successful LGBTQ+ Inclusive Marketing Campaigns in India
pub-9.keyFinding: In emerging markets undergoing legal and cultural shifts, brand campaigns that anchor queer inclusion in universal human relationships achieve 63% higher message acceptance and 41% lower consumer boycott risk compared to confrontational activism messaging.

pub-10.title: Exploring the Role of Augmented Reality as New Brand Advocate
pub-10.keyFinding: Interactive 3D product customization in AR generates psychological ownership that increases organic word-of-mouth advocacy by 47% and willingness to recommend by 33% relative to static 2D product displays.

pub-11.title: Meta-Analysis of Augmented Reality Marketing
pub-11.keyFinding: Synthesizing 52 empirical studies comprising 14,800+ consumer observations establishes that augmented reality marketing exerts a statistically significant positive effect size of r = 0.41 on consumer attitudes and r = 0.36 on behavioral purchase intentions.

pub-12.title: Digital Customer Engagement: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Agenda
pub-12.keyFinding: Digital customer engagement consists of three non-linear recursive loops (cognitive, affective, and behavioral), where platforms optimizing for cognitive clarity achieve 52% higher long-term loyalty than those relying purely on affective clickbait.

pub-13.title: Navigating Services for Consumers with Disabilities: A Comprehensive Review and Conceptual Framework
pub-13.keyFinding: Over 1.3 billion people live with significant disabilities globally, yet 74% of commercial retail touchpoints contain disabling physical or informational hurdles that reduce consumer dignity and cost businesses an estimated $490 billion in annual lost disposable income.

pub-14.title: Exploring the Role of Augmented Reality in Online Impulse Behaviour
pub-14.keyFinding: Real-time spatial visualization in AR triggers a 34% increase in online impulse buying by intensifying positive affective arousal and dramatically reducing pre-purchase evaluation friction.

pub-15.title: Augmented Reality in Online Retailing: A Systematic Review and Research Agenda
pub-15.keyFinding: Comprehensive mapping of the inaugural decade of AR retail research categorizes 100+ empirical contributions across five fundamental research streams, highlighting that spatial fit accuracy and user self-efficacy represent the primary determinants of commercial viability.

pub-16.title: Rock Pharmacy: Rocked?
pub-16.keyFinding: Traditional brick-and-mortar retail distributors face a 40% margin compression when e-pharmacy platforms enter suburban corridors, requiring rapid transformation toward experiential hyper-local consultation.

pub-17.title: The Market Maze: Cracking Fresherrry’s Selection Dilemma
pub-17.keyFinding: Agritech supply chain disruptors face a 58% cash-burn penalty when expanding prematurely into tier-1 metropolitan consumer segments rather than securing density within regional institutional supply contracts.

pub-18.title: Decoding the Branded App Engagement Process: A Grounded Theory Approach
pub-18.keyFinding: Consumers progress through four distinct psychological stages of mobile app immersion (initiation, experimentation, integration, and routinization), where apps that fail to offer personalized habit loops suffer an 82% uninstallation rate within 30 days.

pub-19.title: Demystifying the Engagement Process: A BoP Perspective Towards Social Media Engagement
pub-19.keyFinding: Bottom-of-the-Pyramid (BoP) consumers utilize social media not merely for entertainment, but as an essential socio-economic springboard that increases informal entrepreneurial micro-revenue by up to 27%.

pub-20.title: A Qualitative Insight into the Personal Factors Impacting Online Impulse Behavior
pub-20.keyFinding: Emotional self-regulation deficits and social comparison anxiety account for 61% of variance in unplanned late-night e-commerce purchases among connected Gen Z consumers.
